precepts.text: He sent his word, and healed them, and delivered them from their destructions. You men know what the will of God is; then you're ahead of the whole world. His word is what's going to heal.
precepts.point: The first step of changing is to acknowledge that we have issues.

note.label: Pay The Price: Pleasure Now Regret Later

precepts.why:
Christ said, “They that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick.” He came for the sick, those that need healing. So what do we use to heal ourselves? The psalm answers: “He sent his word, and healed them, and delivered them from their destructions.”

He sent his word down to heal them. Write that down. The word of God is the medicine the physician brings.

So, men, do you know what the will of God is? Then you are ahead of the whole world, because people out here are crazy. People think you can still eat pork, or whatever you do, vote for Trump, whatever people are doing in this world. But you know his word, and his word is what is going to heal.

That is how the sinners at Christ's table were to be made whole: not by sacrifices, but by receiving the word he sent and letting it deliver them from their destructions. We all come in here sick, and we need to get cured.

precepts.text: Such as sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, being bound in affliction and iron; that is the shadow of death, captivity.
precepts.point: The shadow of death is those bound in affliction and iron. So the valley of the shadow of death is America, the valley of dry bones, the Israelites waking up in the presence of their enemies.

note.label: Psalm 23: The Lord Is My Shepherd

precepts.why:
“Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil”. The shadow of death is defined here: “Such as sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, being bound in affliction and iron”.

The shadow of death is those bound in affliction and iron: captivity. So the valley of the shadow of death is America, the valley of dry bones, the Israelites waking up in the presence of their enemies. Walking through it, we fear no evil, for he is with us, and his rod and his staff comfort us.

precepts.text: They that sit in darkness, bound in affliction and iron, because they rebelled against the word; He brought down their heart with labor.
precepts.point: This place is spiritual Egypt. The nations dealt wisely with us and put us to hard labor and bondage, and we are the essential workers on the front line.

note.label: Psalm 44: We Got Not the Land by Our Own Sword

precepts.why:
“Though thou hast sore broken us in the place of dragons, and covered us with the shadow of death.” Psalm 107 shows who sits in that shadow and why: “Such as sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, being bound in affliction and iron; Because they rebelled against the words of God, and contemned the counsel of the most High: Therefore he brought down their heart with labour; they fell down, and there was none to help.”

The broken part is that he brought down their heart with labour and there was none to help. Bound in affliction and iron, in hard labour, because we rebelled against the words of God. Yet the psalm says “yet have we not forgotten thee, neither have we dealt falsely in thy covenant”, and “Our heart is not turned back”; all this came, and still the heart is to hold to him.

precepts.text: The mercy is shown unto thousands of them that love the Most High and keep His commandments.
precepts.point: The mercy is to those that keep His commandments, so His commandments endure forever and they are not going away. This is the same as the grace spoken of in Ephesians 2:8.

note.label: Psalm 107: O Give Thanks unto the Lord

precepts.why:
“for his mercy endureth for ever.” Throughout Psalms and throughout the Bible it says his mercy endures forever, and Exodus 20 shows exactly what that mercy is and who it is for: “shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments.”

The mercy is to those that keep his commandments. If the mercy endures forever, then his commandments endure forever too, and they are not going away.

precepts.text: This grace, this mercy, is the same grace through faith spoken of here.
precepts.point: The mercy is to those that keep His commandments, so His commandments endure forever and they are not going away. This is the same as the grace spoken of in Ephesians 2:8.

note.label: Psalm 107: O Give Thanks unto the Lord

precepts.why:
“For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God”. The mercy that endures forever in the psalm is the same thing as this grace.

The mercy is shown unto them that love the Most High and keep his commandments, and the grace is through faith, the gift of God. Neither one does away with his commandments; the mercy and the grace are for those who keep them, and they endure forever.

precepts.text: Zion, the Israelites, shall be redeemed with judgment and her converts with righteousness, but the transgressors and sinners that forsake the Lord shall be consumed together.
precepts.point: Zion shall be redeemed with judgment, and to be converted you have to be keeping God's laws, His righteousness. When you forsake the Lord's laws you are consumed together with the sinners.

note.label: Psalm 107: O Give Thanks unto the Lord

precepts.why:
“Let the redeemed of the Lord say so, whom he hath redeemed from the hand of the enemy”. Isaiah tells who the redeemed are and how they are redeemed: “Zion shall be redeemed with judgment, and her converts with righteousness.”

Zion is the Israelites, and they are the ones that need to say these things. Zion is redeemed with judgment, and her converts with righteousness, which is keeping God's laws.

“And the destruction of the transgressors and of the sinners shall be together, and they that forsake the Lord shall be consumed.” When you forsake the Lord's laws you are consumed together with the sinners. The redeemed are the ones that did not forsake him.

precepts.text: To be converted you must be keeping God's righteousness, His commandments.
precepts.point: Zion shall be redeemed with judgment, and to be converted you have to be keeping God's laws, His righteousness. When you forsake the Lord's laws you are consumed together with the sinners.

note.label: Psalm 107: O Give Thanks unto the Lord

precepts.why:
Isaiah says Zion's converts are redeemed “with righteousness”, and Deuteronomy defines the righteousness: “it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments before the Lord our God, as he hath commanded us.”

So to be converted you have to be keeping God's laws, his righteousness. That is what makes a man one of the redeemed of the Lord who can say so.

precepts.text: Zion is Israel.
precepts.point: Zion shall be redeemed with judgment, and to be converted you have to be keeping God's laws, His righteousness. When you forsake the Lord's laws you are consumed together with the sinners.

note.label: Psalm 107: O Give Thanks unto the Lord

precepts.why:
“Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel, and all the heads of the tribes, the chief of the fathers of the children of Israel, unto king Solomon in Jerusalem, that they might bring up the ark of the covenant of the Lord out of the city of David, which is Zion.”

Zion is the city of David, and the elders of Israel and all the heads of the tribes are gathered to it. Zion is Israel. So when Isaiah says Zion shall be redeemed with judgment, the redeemed of the Lord in the psalm are the Israelites.

precepts.text: The Redeemer, referring to Christ, shall come to Zion and unto them that turn from transgression in Jacob.
precepts.point: Zion shall be redeemed with judgment, and to be converted you have to be keeping God's laws, His righteousness. When you forsake the Lord's laws you are consumed together with the sinners.

note.label: Psalm 107: O Give Thanks unto the Lord

precepts.why:
“And the Redeemer shall come to Zion, and unto them that turn from transgression in Jacob, saith the Lord.” The Redeemer is Christ, and he comes to Zion, to Israel.

But notice who in Zion he comes to: “them that turn from transgression in Jacob”. That is the same as being redeemed with judgment and converted with righteousness. The redeemed of the Lord, whom he has redeemed from the hand of the enemy, are those in Jacob who turn from transgression and keep his laws.

precepts.text: Wisdom, the unspotted mirror of the power of God, is this Bible, the image of His goodness.
precepts.point: The Bible is the image of His goodness to His people, the Israelites. We are to live by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of the Most High, and eating the word means learning it.

note.label: Psalm 107: O Give Thanks unto the Lord

precepts.why:
“For he satisfieth the longing soul, and filleth the hungry soul with goodness.” The goodness is the word of God, the Bible. Wisdom is described as “the brightness of the everlasting light, the unspotted mirror of the power of God, and the image of his goodness.”

Wisdom, the unspotted mirror of the power of God, is this Bible, and it is the image of his goodness to his people, the Israelites. That is the goodness that fills the hungry soul and the wonderful works to the children of men that men should praise the Lord for.

precepts.text: Man shall not live by bread alone but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God, so we must live by this Bible.
precepts.point: The Bible is the image of His goodness to His people, the Israelites. We are to live by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of the Most High, and eating the word means learning it.

note.label: Psalm 107: O Give Thanks unto the Lord

precepts.why:
“But he answered and said, It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.” The hungry soul in the psalm is filled with goodness, not with bread alone.

We are to live by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of the Most High, so we must live by this Bible. That is how he satisfies the longing soul.

precepts.text: The words were found and eaten, becoming the joy and rejoicing of the heart, so this Bible should be our chief joy.
precepts.point: The Bible is the image of His goodness to His people, the Israelites. We are to live by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of the Most High, and eating the word means learning it.

note.label: Psalm 107: O Give Thanks unto the Lord

precepts.why:
“Thy words were found, and I did eat them; and thy word was unto me the joy and rejoicing of mine heart: for I am called by thy name, O Lord God of hosts.” Jeremiah ate the words of God, and eating the word means learning it.

That is how the hungry soul is filled with goodness: the words are found and eaten, and they become the joy and rejoicing of the heart. This Bible should be our chief joy, because we too are called by his name.

precepts.text: If you will not hearken unto the voice of the Lord to observe and do all His commandments, all these curses shall come upon you and overtake you, and this is why the curses came upon us as a people.
precepts.point: Because we rebelled and hated this Bible, He brought down our heart with labor, He brought down our minds with slavery. We fell down and there was none to help.

note.label: Psalm 107: O Give Thanks unto the Lord

precepts.why:
“Because they rebelled against the words of God, and contemned the counsel of the most High”. That rebellion is exactly what the curses of Deuteronomy 28 are for: “if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes which I command thee this day; that all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee”.

This is why the curses came upon us as a people. We would not hearken to observe and do all his commandments, so all these curses came upon us and overtook us, and we sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, bound in affliction and iron.

precepts.text: These curses are a sign and a wonder upon us and our seed forever, generational curses, because we served not the Lord with joyfulness and gladness of heart, so we serve our enemies in hunger, thirst, and nakedness with a yoke of iron.
precepts.point: Because we rebelled and hated this Bible, He brought down our heart with labor, He brought down our minds with slavery. We fell down and there was none to help.

note.label: Psalm 107: O Give Thanks unto the Lord

precepts.why:
“And they shall be upon thee for a sign and for a wonder, and upon thy seed for ever.” These curses are a sign and a wonder upon us and our seed forever: generational curses. That is why we are still bound in affliction and iron today, in captivity, even as we are raising back up and learning the words of God.

“Because thou servedst not the Lord thy God with joyfulness, and with gladness of heart, for the abundance of all things; Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies which the Lord shall send against thee, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in want of all things: and he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck, until he have destroyed thee.”

The “affliction and iron” of the psalm is this yoke of iron. Because we rebelled against the words of God and hated this Bible, he brought down our heart with labour and our minds with slavery, and we serve our enemies in hunger, thirst and nakedness.

precepts.text: The Lord brings us into Egypt again with ships, sold unto our enemies for bondmen and bondwomen, and no man buys us, identifying the children of Israel as the so-called blacks, Hispanics, and native Indians who went on the slave ships.
precepts.point: Because we rebelled and hated this Bible, He brought down our heart with labor, He brought down our minds with slavery. We fell down and there was none to help.

note.label: Psalm 107: O Give Thanks unto the Lord

precepts.why:
“And the Lord shall bring thee into Egypt again with ships, by the way whereof I spake unto thee, Thou shalt see it no more again: and there ye shall be sold unto your enemies for bondmen and bondwomen, and no man shall buy you.”

This is the captivity the psalm speaks of. The Lord brings us into Egypt again with ships, we are sold unto our enemies for bondmen and bondwomen, and no man buys us. It identifies the children of Israel as the so-called blacks, Hispanics and native Indians who went on the slave ships.

That is how we came to sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, bound in affliction and iron: we “fell down, and there was none to help.”

precepts.text: We grope at noonday as the blind grope in darkness, seeing the truth right in front of us but walking right on by, only oppressed and spoiled evermore with no man to save us.
precepts.point: Because we rebelled and hated this Bible, He brought down our heart with labor, He brought down our minds with slavery. We fell down and there was none to help.

note.label: Psalm 107: O Give Thanks unto the Lord

precepts.why:
“And thou shalt grope at noonday, as the blind gropeth in darkness, and thou shalt not prosper in thy ways: and thou shalt be only oppressed and spoiled evermore, and no man shall save thee.”

This is the darkness of the psalm. We grope at noonday as the blind grope in darkness, seeing the truth right in front of us but walking right on by. We are only oppressed and spoiled evermore, and “there was none to help”: no man to save us.

precepts.text: The Most High returns to His place until we acknowledge our offense and seek His face; in our affliction we will seek Him early, so sometimes affliction is good for our people that we may seek the Lord.
precepts.point: He brought them out of darkness and the shadow of death and brake their bands asunder. He broke the gates of brass and cut the bars of iron in sunder, taking away our captivity.

note.label: Psalm 107: O Give Thanks unto the Lord

precepts.why:
“Then they cried unto the Lord in their trouble, and he saved them out of their distresses.” Hosea shows what has to happen first: “I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.”

The Most High returns to his place until we acknowledge our offence, the wrong we did in breaking God's laws, and seek his face. That is when he begins to save us, bringing us out of darkness and the shadow of death and breaking our bands in sunder.

“in their affliction they will seek me early.” So sometimes affliction is good for our people, that we may seek the Lord. Then he breaks the gates of brass and cuts the bars of iron in sunder, taking away our captivity.

precepts.text: In the wilderness the angels' food agreed to every taste, whatever your delight was it tasted like, yet we still complained as a people.
precepts.point: They draw near unto the gates of death, then they cry unto the Lord in their trouble and He saveth them. He sent His word and healed them, so we get healed today by God's word.

note.label: Psalm 107: O Give Thanks unto the Lord

precepts.why:
“Their soul abhorreth all manner of meat; and they draw near unto the gates of death.” In the wilderness the Most High “feddest thine own people with angels’ food, and didst send them from heaven bread prepared without their labour, able to content every man’s delight, and agreeing to every taste.”

The angels' food agreed to every taste: whatever your delight was, it tasted like that. Yet we still complained as a people, and our soul abhorred all manner of meat. That shows how stiffnecked we were even in the wilderness, and why the Bible calls us fools who are afflicted because of our transgression and our iniquities.

precepts.text: The poor in spirit are blessed, and it is they whom the Most High sets on high from affliction.
precepts.point: Whoso is wise and will observe these things, even they shall understand the lovingkindness of the Lord. If you have wisdom you will observe these things.

note.label: Psalm 107: O Give Thanks unto the Lord

precepts.why:
“Yet setteth he the poor on high from affliction, and maketh him families like a flock.” The poor here are the poor in spirit. “Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.”

The poor in spirit are blessed, and it is they whom the Most High sets on high from affliction. The righteous, those keeping God's commandments, shall see it and rejoice, and all iniquity shall stop her mouth.

precepts.text: Prosperity and adversity, life and death, poverty and riches all come of the Lord; you prospered one time and now you are in your season of adversity.
precepts.point: Whoso is wise and will observe these things, even they shall understand the lovingkindness of the Lord. If you have wisdom you will observe these things.

note.label: Psalm 107: O Give Thanks unto the Lord

precepts.why:
“Prosperity and adversity, life and death, poverty and riches, come of the Lord.” All of it comes of him.

That is the psalm: “Again, they are minished and brought low through oppression, affliction, and sorrow”, meaning we go back into slavery, and yet he sets the poor on high from affliction. You prospered one time, and now you are in your season of adversity. Whoso is wise and will observe these things will understand the lovingkindness of the Lord in both.

precepts.text: Children are the heritage and gift of the Lord, one of the things we understand come of Him.
precepts.point: Whoso is wise and will observe these things, even they shall understand the lovingkindness of the Lord. If you have wisdom you will observe these things.

note.label: Psalm 107: O Give Thanks unto the Lord

precepts.why:
“Lo, children are an heritage of the Lord: and the fruit of the womb is his reward.” He “maketh him families like a flock”; children are the heritage and gift of the Lord.

This is one of the things we understand come of him. Whoso is wise and will observe these things understands the lovingkindness of the Lord.

precepts.text: Fools because of their transgression, and because of their iniquities, are afflicted; when we break God's laws he calls us fools.
precepts.point: Many a time have they afflicted me from my youth, yet they have not prevailed against me. Israel is afflicted because of sin, but the affliction has not prevailed, because we have been in and out of captivity through repentance.

note.label: Psalm 129: Many a Time Have They Afflicted Me

precepts.why: “Many a time have they afflicted me from my youth”. Israel is afflicted because of sin: “Fools because of their transgression, and because of their iniquities, are afflicted.” When we break God’s laws he calls us fools, and the affliction follows the transgression.

precepts.text: Fools because of their transgression and their iniquities are afflicted.
precepts.point: We get afflicted because of our sins, and the Most High calls us fools. Yet these scriptures were written for our learning so that through patience we might have hope.

note.label: Psalm 132: The Oath to David and the Throne Forever

precepts.why:
“Lord, remember David, and all his afflictions”. The affliction refers to David’s sins. If you know David’s history, he did foolish things, got one of his best men killed and took his wife. “Fools because of their transgression, and because of their iniquities, are afflicted.”

We get afflicted because of our sins, and the Most High calls us fools. Yet these scriptures were written for our learning, so that through patience we might have hope.

precepts.text: Such as sit in darkness and the shadow of death, bound in affliction and iron, are the scattered Israelites.
precepts.point: "Galilee of the Gentiles" proves the point, because those northern tribes of Zebulun and Naphtali, broken and driven into darkness, are the people who saw the great light when Christ came preaching, "Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand." They sat in the shadow of death because Ephraim was broken and taken into Assyria.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“Such as sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, being bound in affliction and iron.”

Those that sit in darkness and the shadow of death, bound in affliction and iron, are the scattered Israelites. That is the same people of whom Matthew says, “to them which sat in the region and shadow of death light is sprung up.”

points: Give thanks unto the Lord for He is good, for His mercy endureth forever. Throughout Psalms and throughout the Bible it says His mercy endures forever, and the teaching stops to show exactly what that mercy is.
The mercy is to those that keep His commandments, so His commandments endure forever and they are not going away. This is the same as the grace spoken of in Ephesians 2:8.

points: He gathers the redeemed out of the lands from the east and from the west, from the north and from the south. The ones being gathered are the redeemed, those that are keeping God's commandments.

points: They wandered in the wilderness in a solitary way and found no city to dwell in, hungry and thirsty, their soul fainting in them. Then they cried unto the Lord in their trouble and He delivered them out of their distresses.

note.label: Psalm 107: O Give Thanks unto the Lord

note.label: Psalm 107: O Give Thanks unto the Lord

points: Let them sacrifice the sacrifices of thanksgiving and declare His works with rejoicing. They that go down to the sea in ships and do business in great waters see the works of the Lord and His wonders in the deep.

points: He commandeth and raiseth the stormy wind which lifteth up the waves, referring to hurricanes that mount up to heaven and go down again to the depths, and the sailors' souls are melted because of trouble as they reel and stagger like a drunken man at their wits' end.
